title: Early years in the Mississippi valley states, no attention to music
summary: He lived at home until 16, then worked in Arkansas, Missouri, Illinois and Tennessee, paying no attention to music until he came to New Orleans. An interviewer aside clarifies they want the Bolden period.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: I see. And were you raised up there?
And where did you come then?
Oh, I was up to Arkansas, Missouri, Illinois, Tennessee.
What kind of music did you hear in Mississippi then?
I don't pay no attention to music yet. All right.
And did you hear any music in all these other different states, Arkansas, Missouri?
No, I wasn't paying no attention to music yet. I didn't pay no attention to music until I come down here.
Oh, I see. What kind of work were you doing in Arkansas and Missouri?

Little camp. I thought y'all was getting the music directors of here. Y'all got to go way back, go to work, catch the music and things. I thought y'all didn't want to pick up the music here from Buddy Bowman. No, we wasn't going to ask about that. We wanted to get the difference. We got to go way back then and way bone that and everything like that. I don't think that sounds so hot. We just wondered how old, you see, he was. So we know just which period that he lived here. It was about 1890 then, I guess, when you moved here. No, no, no.
